punchline: A split-brain patient explained a shovel by the chicken shed, and Haidt says your own reasoning often does the same: it explains what the elephant already chose.
thirty_sec: Haidt first rode a horse alone in 1991. On a steep trail that turned sharply left he froze, and the horse and its neighbour simply turned. He took it as an image of the mind: a small rider on a big elephant. Gazzaniga's split-brain patient even explained a shovel as being for the chicken shed. Arguing with the elephant fails, so change what it meets: remove the temptation, make the right path easy.
